links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT vs AGA patient education materials
links.effect: Mean FKGL was higher for ChatGPT than GI website materials (10.33 ± 1.5 vs 8.72 ± 1.7; mean difference 1.61; P < .001).
links.quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was higher for ChatGPT than GI website materials (10.33 ± 1.5 vs 8.72 ± 1.7; mean difference, 1.61; P < .001).

links.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT-generated patient education relative to appropriate patient reading level
links.effect: ChatGPT text averaged grade 10.33 versus 8.72 for AGA materials, a significantly higher reading level.
links.quote: ChatGPT-generated gastrointestinal patient education demonstrated similar quality, understandability, and actionability compared with professional society materials but was written at a significantly higher reading level.

screen.reason: Evaluates readability, quality, understandability, and actionability of ChatGPT-generated GI patient education materials against standard professional society materials without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
